question.text: According to FATF Special Recommendation VIII (SR VIII), non-profit organisations (NPOs) are considered "particularly vulnerable" to terrorist financing abuse. Which of the following vulnerabilities must countries specifically address through their laws and regulations?

answer.text: All of: (i) terrorist organisations posing as legitimate NPOs, (ii) exploitation of legitimate NPOs as conduits for TF, and (iii) concealment of clandestine diversion of funds to terrorist organisations
Only terrorist organisations posing as legitimate NPOs and exploitation of legitimate NPOs as conduits
Only concealment of clandestine diversion of funds to terrorist organisations
Only exploitation of legitimate NPOs as conduits for terrorist financing and tax evasion through NPOs

explanation.text: The Logic: SR VIII identifies three specific NPO vulnerabilities to terrorist financing abuse that countries must address: (i) terrorist organisations posing as legitimate entities, (ii) exploitation of legitimate entities as conduits for terrorist financing, and (iii) concealment or obscuring of the clandestine diversion of funds intended for legitimate purposes to terrorist organisations. All three must be addressed. The Trap: Partial lists are tempting because each individual vulnerability sounds complete on its own. SR VIII requires all three to be addressed, and tax evasion is not part of SR VIII. Note: SR VIII frames NPOs as "particularly vulnerable" to TF and groups the vulnerabilities as: posing-as-legitimate, conduit exploitation, and clandestine fund diversion.
